answers.goal: Grades runs on the CRM end state, not the closing message; seeds tool failures and timeouts at the last write; counts false successes apart; labels the first failing step in a last-success by first-failure matrix; turns the 7 runs into regression tasks.

Writes tasks with a starting state, an end-state check in a sandbox and forbidden events (refund over 200 EUR without approval, double refund, refund on an order not found), fixes k before the run, reports pass^k and states the rule-of-three bound on zero forbidden events.

Refuses pass@3 as the gate for payments that cannot be undone, asks for the per-trial rate and pass^k (0.9 per trial gives about 0.73 over 3), says zero wrong payments in 30 trials still allows about 10%, up to about 120 payments a month, and keeps the approval.

Grades runs on the CRM end state, not the closing message; seeds tool failures and timeouts at the last write; counts false successes apart; labels the first failing step in a last-success by first-failure matrix; turns the 7 runs into regression tasks.

Refuses the 0 of 120 as evidence because the filter was adjusted on those same emails and asks for an attack set kept apart from tuning; plants injections inside the 300 real client emails so benign utility, utility under attack and attack success rate come from the same tasks; reads attack success per forbidden action (contact change, documents sent outside) with its upper bound, about 2.5% for 0 of 120.
